components.css: .ds-world-lav { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #6470CC, #5563C2, #3D48A4); padding: 24px; border-radius: 0; } .ds-btn-primary-lav { font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 16px; color: #FFFFFF; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #7458E8, #5638CC); box-shadow: inset 0px 1px 0px rgba(255,255,255,0.55); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), background-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), opacity 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); } .ds-btn-primary-lav:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-btn-primary-lav:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary-lav:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FFFFFF; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-world-stone { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #6E6C5A, #4F4E43, #36362D); padding: 24px; border-radius: 0; } .ds-bar-stone { display: flex; padding: 6px; height: 72px; box-sizing: border-box; border-radius: 30px; background: linear-gradient(rgba(24,24,18,0.36), rgba(24,24,18,0.36)), linear-gradient(rgba(52,51,42,0.56), rgba(52,51,42,0.56)); backdrop-filter: blur(28px) saturate(1.1); border: 1px solid; border-top-color: rgba(255,247,228,0.42); border-left-color: rgba(255,247,228,0.22); border-right-color: rgba(255,247,228,0.07); border-bottom-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.28); box-shadow: 6px 20px 44px -12px rgba(14,13,8,0.40), 1px 2px 6px rgba(14,13,8,0.20); } .ds-tab-stone { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 3px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 24px; background: transparent; color: #F1ECE0; font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), background 220ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); } .ds-tab-stone-on { color: #FFFBE9; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,246,226,0.14), rgba(255,246,226,0.08)); border-color: rgba(255,247,228,0.08); border-top-color: rgba(255,247,228,0.45); box-shadow: 2px 6px 14px -6px rgba(14,13,8,0.45); } .ds-tab-stone:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-tab-stone:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FFFBE9; outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Trail (every look; Paper shown)
components.description: Today's trail, the same object in all four looks, drawn from each look's tokens (node, onNode, trailWalked, trailAhead, nodeAhead, nodeAheadFill, nodeCurrentFill); Paper shown. A footpath of dots, the walked part dense and strong, the way ahead sparser and fainter. The node shows the step's state (a filled node when done, a lit ring with a breathing halo for the step up next, a waypoint ahead, a flag at the summit). Each card is the tap target: one tap ticks it (or adds one to a counter), long press edits; it ends in a 26dp check ring that fills with the kind colour. The step up next is lit and its meta line reads in text ink. A done card recedes, its pebble dims to 60% and its title goes faint with a line through it.
components.css: .ds-world-paper { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #F8F7F3, #EEEFEA, #E4E7E1); padding: 24px; border-radius: 0; font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-trail-paper { position: relative; } .ds-trail-paper-rail { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; } .ds-step-paper { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 5px 0; } .ds-node-col { width: 44px; height: 34px; flex: none; display: grid; place-items: center; position: relative; } .ds-node-paper-done { width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 15px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #2F3A33; color: #FFFFFF; narrative.overview:
Every surface in Routine is a pane of glass held up to a world, and that world has its own weather and its own light. The light never stops moving: a rose and an azure orb circle slowly behind Lavender, a beam of window light sways across Stone's room, a low sun and a band of mist drift over Paper's mountains, a moon glow wanders over Pine's canopy. The glass catches that light as it passes, so a list of chores feels like looking out of a window at a particular hour, not like filling in a form. The person picks the hour that suits them in Settings, and each one is a complete world: its own backdrop, its own glass, its own type voice, its own reward. Underneath, every look is the same app: the same screens, with the same components in the same order and the same places, doing the same things.

What stays the same across all four is the physics. There is one glass material with a fixed stack of layers and a fixed set of tiers; one light clock that runs at the root of the app; one motion grammar where every change of state fades, eases or springs and nothing ever cuts; one contrast gate that rebuilds each look pixel by pixel and refuses any text under 4.5:1. The four looks are four tunings of the same instrument. A new screen should be designed once against the shared system, then voiced per look through tokens, never forked into four layouts. A look may differ only in its colours, its glass material, its backdrop and header art, its typeface and weights, and the small radius and rim details its tokens carry.

The density is calm and single-column: one thing per pane, generous 16px gutters, one primary action per screen, and the "what do I do now?" answer at the top of every screen. The feel is quiet, lit and tactile, never techy. Rejected outright: generic dashboard tiles, decorative glass, grey text on grey glass, illustration that reads as clip-art or as a stock AI picture (the lone figure in a portal and the drawn magnolia were both removed for this reason), and any mark that scolds the person for what they missed.
keyCharacteristics: One glass material with six tiers (hero, pane, control, inset, sheet, chrome), tuned per look through `colors.material`.
A world behind the glass: a rendered backdrop, a pre-blurred lens image, and moving light layers on one shared clock.
Done and skipped things recede into the world (a done title goes faint with a line through it); the one thing up next is lit.
Text contrast of at least 4.5:1 everywhere, enforced by a script against the real pixels, not by eye.
Every change of state fades, eases or springs; nothing cuts. Most run 120 to 320ms on one ease-out; rewards and progress take longer. Reduced motion drops travel and keeps fades.
One layout per screen in every look: the looks differ in colour, material, backdrop and header art and type, never in what is shown or where.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every text token must reach 4.5:1 on the real pixels behind it: lens, base, body, caustics, top glow, sheen, the moving light at its brightest point on its path, and grain. Unchecked outlines (`controlBorder`) must reach 3:1 against the glass itself, and kind fills and the accent 3:1 against their track. `python3 scripts/check-contrast.py` checks this for all four looks (362 checks at the time of writing) and must pass after any change to tokens, material, art or `assets/art/looks.json`. Judging contrast by eye on a screenshot is not enough, because the light moves.

rules.name: The Dim the Light Rule
rules.body: When text fails the gate, dim or move the backdrop light (the art, the scrim, the light layer's strength). Never thicken the glass to rescue it. Thick glass hides the world, and the world is the point.

rules.name: The Roles Not Hues Rule
rules.body: Screens use roles (`text`, `muted`, `link`, `primary`, `doneFill`, `kinds.gym.text`), never a literal colour. A literal in a screen file means the other three looks are wrong.

rules.name: The Meaningful Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour carries meaning: the kind of thing, done, up next, the streak, an error. Decorative colour is not added. On Paper this is strictest: everything that is not a kind, the streak or an error is ink, so Paper's section dots and hub section marks are dropped or drawn in ink.

rules.name: The No Grey on Grey Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is a tinted near-ink of the look (Lilac Breath, Linen, Graphite, Sage Mist) chosen to pass on that look's glass, never a neutral grey laid on grey glass. A disabled or receded state is shown by opacity, faint ink and the line through a done title, not by a grey wash.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (counts, times, weights, timers, progress) uses tabular figures, so nothing jitters as it ticks.

rules.name: The Mono Is for Numerals Rule
rules.body: Mono appears only in Pine, and only for numerals. Words, labels and phrases such as "4 in a row" or "40 kg × 8" are set in the sans with tabular figures. Mono is never used to make something look technical. The one other use is the backup code field, which holds a machine code people copy character by character, so a fixed-width face is doing real work there.

rules.name: The Sixteen Floor Rule
rules.body: Reading text is 16px and secondary lines are 14px; no sentence is ever set smaller. Below 14px sit only short marks that are not sentences: labels and captions (13; Paper's labels stay at 14), counts in segments, chips, ticks and badges (13), tab labels (13 on Lavender, 12 elsewhere), status pills (Paper Bold 12, Pine Bold 11 capitals) and the counter inside a 24px check box (12). Nothing goes below 11px.

rules.name: The One Material Rule
rules.body: Every surface draws from the look's `colors.material`. No screen invents its own fill, border or shadow for a card, button or control.

rules.name: The Glass Earns Its Place Rule
rules.body: Glass holds content or a control. A pane with nothing to say, a frame around a frame, or glass added because glass is pretty, is removed.

rules.name: The Light Comes From the World Rule
rules.body: Light direction is fixed per look: Stone's from the window at the top left (shadows fall down-right), Pine's from the moon (the sheen rises from below), Lavender's and Paper's from above. New shadows and highlights follow the look's light.

rules.name: The Recede, Don't Scold Rule
rules.body: Finished and skipped things sink back into the world: faint ink, a thinner body, a dimmed tile. A done title takes one quiet line through it, a record of the thing done, never a red mark. Nothing turns red or shouts about a missed day; a skipped step says "Skipped · streak kept".

dos: **Do** re-render the art with `python3 scripts/render-art.py <look>` after any change to `assets/art/looks.json` or the art code (the lens is a pre-blurred copy baked from them), then run `python3 scripts/check-contrast.py` and keep it passing. Run the gate after any change to tokens or material too. Text 4.5:1; unchecked outlines 3:1 against the glass; kind fills and the accent 3:1 against their track.
**Do** fix a contrast failure by dimming or moving the backdrop light. Never by thickening the glass.
**Do** make every touch target at least 44 by 44 with at least 8px between targets.
**Do** give every icon-only button an `accessibilityLabel`, and every tick an `accessibilityRole` of checkbox with its checked state.
**Do** keep focus rings: 2px in the text colour on pressable surfaces and 1.5px around fields on Android, `:focus-visible` on the web. Never remove them.
**Do** keep reading text at 16px and secondary lines at 14px; go smaller only for the short marks the Sixteen Floor Rule lists.
**Do** use Ionicons for icons, drawn in role colours.
**Do** make every action reachable by tap or long press with a screen-reader action as well; nothing relies on hover.
**Do** fade, ease or spring every change of state (selection 150ms, press 120 and 160ms, ease-out).
**Do** put a visible label above every input.
**Do** keep the bottom navigation at five items or fewer.
**Do** respect the system's reduced-motion setting through `useReduceMotion()`: drop transforms, keep fades.

**Do** keep the saved data keys (`routine.routines.v1`, `routine.gym.v1`, `routine.chinese.v1`, `routine.groceries.v1`, `routine.settings.v1`, `routine.journal.v1`, `routine.inbox.v1`) and their data shapes compatible through any redesign.

**Do** build a new screen from the shared kit (`Glass`, `Press`, `Button`, `Chip`, `Segmented`, `Field`, `Section`, `PageTitle`, `Sheet`, `Fab`, the motion pieces), branch on the material's `canopy`, `tag` and `orb` rather than on look names (never on `theme.glass`: every screen has one layout), and check it in all four looks.
**Do** let done things recede (faint ink, a line through a done title, a dimmed tile, a thinner body) and the one next thing be lit.
**Do** keep secondary text in the look's own tinted near-ink; never set grey text on grey glass.
donts: **Don't** change any state in 0ms. A cut is never the reduced form of motion; a fade is.
**Don't** use a placeholder as the only label.

**Don't** put eyebrow chips (small tag pills above a title that announce a section or a category). Two pills are allowed because they carry the item's own state: the status pill in a Library card's top row ("3 in a row", "Today", "Resting", "Skipped"), and Pine's tags beside or under a name ("Up next · 21:00", "New best").
**Don't** use glass as pure decoration: a pane must hold content or a control.
**Don't** add a coloured stripe thicker than 1px down one side of a card as an accent.
**Don't** use mono as a costume. Mono is Pine's numerals only.
**Don't** build hero-metric stat tiles (a big number, a small label, a trend arrow, in a grid). Stats are told in a sentence and a chart, as on "Your week".
**Don't** use clip-art or stock AI-style illustration: no lone figure in a glowing portal, no drawn magnolia. The worlds are light, mist, landscape and photographed material.
**Don't** invent a colour, font or shadow in a screen file; add the token to `src/theme.ts` for all four looks.
**Don't** let glass nested in glass keep its own lens and shadow; it is inset.
**Don't** add specks, stars or dots to a backdrop where they can read as stray UI between panes.
